akkhadhutta.p: [Akkha+dhutta.] (pu) CL=9 Destroying welfare or wealth  by playing games of dice-gambling. Play games of dice excessively.  A person who destroys the wealth or benefit by gambling ,playing excessive games of dice.  See also Akkhanimitta
a: အက္ခဓုတ္တ(ပု)

DOP: 2 akkha m. [ S. akṣa 2 ], 1. a die; dice ; Abh 532; Vin II 10, 20 (~ena pi kīḷanti; Sp 621, 12 : ~enā ti guḷena); D II 348, 19 (dve akkhadhuttā ~ehi dibbiṃsu); S I 149, 24* (yo ~esu dhanaparājayo); Ja V 155, 23* (~assa phalakaṃ); VI 318, 30* (tam āyam ~ehi ajesi jūte); — 2. the name of a tree, Terminalia bellerica, beleric myrobalan ( the seeds of which were used as dice ); Abh 569; Samantak 734 (kaṇhavaṇṭakkhaciñcā); — 3. a certain weight ; Abh 479 (~o māsakā pañca); — °- kkhāyikachātaka , m. or n. , the famine when the seeds of beleric myrobalan were eaten ; Mhv 32:29 (~e); — °- devi(n) , m. , a dice-player, a gambler; Abh 531; — °- dhutta , m. , a gambler; one addicted to dicing ; Abh 531; M III 170, 7 (~o … puttaṃ pi jīyetha); Sn 106 (itthidhutto surādhutto ~o ca yo naro); Ja VI 274, 10* ; — ifc see kūṭ’- ( sv kūṭa 2 ); — °- mālā , f. , a string of seeds, a rosary ; Mhv 46:17 (ekāvaliṃ gahetvāna ~aṃ akā kira); 57:6; — anakkha , m ( fn )., (one) who is not a gambler ; Ja V 117, 31´ (anakkhākitave ti ~e akitave ajūtakare c’ eva akeraṭike ca).
CPD: akkha-dhutta , m. [ sa. akṣa-dhūrta], a gambler, dice-player , Abh 531; Sn 106 (itthidhutta, surā- dhutta, +), Ja lll 58, 9 ' ( do. ); MN ll 106, 24 (~ā akkhehi dibbanti); lll 170, 7 ; 178, 3 ; DN ll 348, 20 (~o kaliṃ gilati); lll 183, 20 ; Ja l 379, 23 (= Bodhi- satto); Vl 274, 10* ( a partner in gambling ). — lfc. v. kūṭa °.
NCP: masculine a gamble; one addicted to dicing See also: akkha
